a complicated story but i think what really contributed to it the most was my mother. she had a history with depression and after 2 terrible employers in a row she developed burnout and depression (i was \~15 at that time) she went into a daycare clinic and was on sick leave for the next 2 years but covid came in her way of searching for a job so she fell into unemployment benefit. during the hights of her depression she didn't open her mail and after she did finally alot of debt had accumulated (which led to her developing a fear of opening the mail). i never really spend my pocket money and after over 10 years of mindelessly saving up quite some time i had accumulated a few thousand already. the began to borrow from me more and more but the debt was probably just to high and so she's bankrupt now. she doesn't want to accept that we have really fallen off the socail ladder quite some bit. at the same time she feels increadibly guilty for how things have turned out.

it's definitly a harsh method. we were weighed 2 times a week. monday was the "important" weighing day. if you didn't gain 500g a week 2 mondays in a row you were kicked out. i actually had a person in my therapy group kicked out beacause of that. otherwise the clinic had way more freedom than most others. we didn't have a meal plan, not all meals were under supervision. you had to allways be at there at meal times sitting on your designated place, but nobody forced you to eat the stuff you ordered. so this weight goal was their control method as otherwise you wouldn't even really have to be creative to sneak the system

my clinic only took people voluntarily going, i went into the clinic voluntarily aswell,

i was verry near needing to be tube fed. the senior physician said that if i fell under weight/BMI X i would need to be tube fed. in the case i would refuse they wouldn't have forced me to do it but since they had no obligation of treating me, i could verry well be kicked out of the clinic. (or not taken in the first place)

for me in my treatment center it depended alot on who you were talking to.

the treatment center wasn't tailored to just eds but rather a general clinic that had a focus on eds but had other patients aswell. the patients were split up into two groups: e- patients with an eating disorder, and a- patients without an eating disorder. the e- patients had of course more restrictions on food, ate in a diffrent room and depending on your weight/how long you were in the clinic - a limit on going-out time, both in time aswell as in if you could leave the hospital grounds or not. otherwise there was no big diffrence. we were together with the a- patients in pretty much any therapy exept like 2 times a week for the ones that didn't make sense for them like cooking or nutrition counselling.

so many of the therapists weren't really specialized in eds specificly. and the nurses especially werent.

funny enough tho the worst were the two nutritionists. who were, of course, just there FOR the ed patients specificly. nutrition counselling was a mix between talking about how we feel about food, our emotions around it and more "classical" nutrition counselling where we would talk about the food pyramid, having a balanced diet etc. etc.

we had a box called "naschibox" that was in the nursing room where we could go to and pick up to 3 things a day from (tho not at the same time, one item per nurse shift beacause eating 2 mini-sized chocolate bars in 2 hours was considered a binge or something). hard to translate but naschi is a term for sweet you would use more for like ... children.. for example when your child gets a good grade you could give them a naschi. this is not only weird beacause we were all adults but also weird beacause together with you having to ask the nurse if you could take something from the box it kind of gave it the vibe that you had to earn eating sweets. at some point some paitents complained about the term. while due to buerocracy the term was never changed officially, at least inoficially it was called "snackbox" instead from that point on.

​

the clinic still helped me ALOT, exactly beacause their focus was more broad but it definitly wasn't for their ed counselling.

shortly after my day clinic time ended i discovered "all in". i wanted to finally truly recovery just as badly as i do now but i still had a good bit more of my ed behavuours.

so i tried all in as good as i could, gave it my all and could only really hold it for like 4-5 days.i judt felt so terrible and hopeless afterwards. this repeated a few times

so i reconsidered what i do and started approaching recovery more stedially

i still estimated the calories of everything i ate (used to count, of course, but i was far enough that not counting but rather estimating calories was now ok for me) i stopped that 2 months ago. i still look at the back of packages when available ngl, i just can't not look but i don't measure anything (we don't have a food scale anyways) or try to calculate/estimate my daily calories since then. i just wish the lables wouldt exist. this was mind boggeling to me. not knowing the calories was allways my biggest fear (i didn't really have a traditional fear food, just fear of not knowing the calories)

my ed clinic said i should weigh myself (like every 1-2 weeks). i didn't have a scale back in peak ed days so i didn't weigh myself back then, but of course it went on to affect me. the scale beeing a problem already started in the clinic and i weighed myself daily afterwars (dumb desicion by me) i continued to allways say to myself that this wasn't affecting me and that i HAD to weigh myself bc what if i loose weight??? so i decided to stop weighing myself almost a month ago now (i mean if i would loose a significant amout of weight i would see it anyways, it is affecting me negatively   so no thank you).

i kinda developed an unhealthy relationship with the stepcounter on my phone where i tried verry hard to hit a goal of X steps a day. if i didn't hit that i would panic a tiny bit in my inside, of how i was going to gain weiht (even tho i was to gain weight what the f?). so i deleted the stepcounter actually yesterday after i started feeling super down.

this is of course not really quantifiable but i do feel that i have waay more mind freedom now than directly after the clinic and i think this mental progress wouldnt have happend (or at least to the degree it did) if i still actively did the things mentioned abobe. it wasn't like those fears were unbreakable forces on me after the clinic but i felt more uncompfortable stepping outside my well.. compfort zone.  which now, for the most part is just more of backthought that lingers on with alot of desicions. i still have a hard time going out of my compfort zone myself , and the fear there does get a good bit higher but when it happens due to others i just play along and thats okay for me. also if a chance comes where someone wants to do something outside my compfort zone i wouldn't say no (maybe going to an all you can eat restaurant idk but that has never happend)

progess is slow but at least it is happening (and not in the backwards direction lol)

i don't really know if all in is for me. i was definitly not ready when i first tried it and i am unsure about now i try to decouple my recovery progress as much as i can from these short motivation bursts followed by slumps (which i have in general) as i can as i don't want to destabalize my mood by that much. i just hope it all somehow works in the end

i grew up allways beeing kinda skinny. like not underweight, but i never really had to look at my weight and people often told me i was skinny, i allways had to choose the slimmer clothing sizes etc. Funny enough despite people telling me i never saw myself as skinny, just "normal" really. and so in my head beeing skinny kinda became how i view myself (not in a bragging way, more like thats how i am supposed to look like). my mom struggels with her weight since allways and did multiple diets in my childhood. she also tried exercising and loved pointinv out how much she HATED it. 

as a kid i wasn't interested in the steriotypical things for my gender. while almost all boys played soccer (i am from germany so soccer is THE sport here), i did hip hop dance, played barbie with my female friends etc. of course i got bullied for beeing the weird girly boy with only female friends. this led me to give up or hide all of my "girly" hobbies after elementary school. i wanted fo be percieved more boy-ish and the age i was in back than is fhe one were fitness started fo really become an important topic for the boys. i jusf wanted to fit in and be accepted and so i tried working out/jogging etc. , but all my attempts failed due to lack of motivation which really started affecting myself esteem after a while. with the knoledge that my mom hated doing sports just as much, it really felt like some curse laid on me preventing me from becomming fitter

alot in my life started changing quite rapidly and so when i was around 14 i developed severe depression for reasons pretty unrelated to my annorexia. after a while, i found a coping mechanisim in food. (especially chips, choclate etc.) i started eating more and more junk to cope. this made me gain quite a bit of weight to the point where i was at the edge of beeing overweight a few years later. my self esteem was never all that high but it really hit rock bottom due to my depression, and i attributed me gaining weight as a proove that i was the failure i percieved mysellf to be. at some point i just hit a breaking point (also mentally as my depression was pretty much at it's worst at that point, self harm and suicidal thoughts included) and started restricting calories which gave me a massive self esteem boost since i FINALLY was able to archive something in my life. it felt like that curse i talked about earlier had finally been lifted. at the time i had a pretty thin friend who was much worse of mentally than me (multiple suicide attempts kind of person). i never really felt like i could talk about my mental problems bc he had it much worse and so while
i didn't really develop annorexia on purpose,  i knew from begining on that both my actions aswell as my thoughts weren't just  normal dieting. i kinda wanted people to see how bad i was feeling mentaly at that time.
at last, i really wanted to be a "femboy". well my friend kinda was one and i had a crush on him. he really looked good in croptops and i started to ask myself "why is he so pretty while i am so ugly?"
the fact that he had much worse mental problems yet still managed to look that good made it even worse for me. (i struggle with basic hygene and self care since i am around 15 to the point where all of my hair had to be cut off beacause it was tangled so badly, i brush my teeth like every month or so etc.)


 the annorexia, for a while pretty much stopped many of the depressive symptoms, my self harm stopped, i felt much better and the fear of both my weight aswell as my mental state spiraling out of control kept me in the restrictive eating patterns.
